name: BYD
h1: Run a fast-growing network from one connected layer
lede: With dealer and service capacity scaling quickly, operations need one shared view across sales, service and parts.
why_h2: Why now for BYD in Australia
why_p: Public reporting shows rapid volume growth and a dealer network that is still being built out.

signals.title: Dealer network heading to about 200 sites
signals.body: Around 120 sales and service sites today, with about 30 more planned by end of 2026 and about 50 in early 2027. Service booking waits are around seven days against a four to five day target.
signals.angle: Hitting service-wait targets across a growing network takes shared scheduling, parts and capacity visibility.

signals.title: Record June deliveries, nearly level with Toyota
signals.body: BYD delivered a record 18,881 vehicles in June, 243 behind Toyota, with the range grown from one model to 12 and almost 140,000 sold in four years.
signals.angle: Volume at this pace needs connected launch, dealer and customer-experience workflows rather than spreadsheets.

signals.title: 2025 deliveries up 156% to 52,415
signals.body: BYD recorded 52,415 deliveries in 2025, up from 20,458 in 2024, and expects to exceed 150 dealers in 2026.
signals.angle: Hypergrowth multiplies handoffs between marketing, sales, service and finance teams.
